prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform alias Cedarbell (coordination only; shares regional context each cycle; receives confirmed capacity impacts). Parts: Demand Prediction Service alias Marlinstone (refreshes stand demand when Ramp Movement Board records material off-block change); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; recalculates from confirmed airport position); Slot Allocation Engine; Airport CDM Portal alias Foxglove (duty confirmations as annotations); Digital Briefing Room; Tower Sequence Manager (receives ramp intent via sync); Ramp Movement Board (apron movements, conflicts, towing, stand occupancy); Departure Metering Service; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console (fallback if Foxglove down); Weather Ingest Gateway alias Orchard; Flight Data Exchange; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Airline Interface Adapter; Alert Distribution Hub (approved duty alerts); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service (authorizes duty confirmations, logs to ledger); Business Rules Registry; Time Synchronization Service; Collaborative Decision Log; East/West Apron Sensors (supporting evidence); runway meters; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector (alerts Ramp Control Lead of stand/service-lane overlaps); Handling Resource Planner (baggage, catering, cleaning, boarding, towing resources); Common Situation Display. Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin; Airline Operations Coordinator alias Saffron (Flight Intent Message, Target Off Block Time; joins resequences affecting boarding/connections/rotation); Aircraft Operator Representative (accepts revised off-block expectations); Slot Coordinator (Calculated Takeoff Time); Airport Duty Manager (Airport Capacity Plan; status confirmation point; Runway Inspection Note; verifies checks before Acceptance Rate/metering changes); Tower Supervisor alias Brindle (verifies runway reductions; confirms pushback integration); Ramp Control Lead alias Quartzline (sequences pushbacks/tows; reconciles sensors; sends Stand Tow Request Form; coordinates conflicts with Ground Handling Dispatcher; reviews Planner constraints; escalates apron congestion affecting runway to Brindle+Duty Manager); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Meteorology Briefing Officer (Storm Cell Snapshot); Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer. Flows: Flight Intent Message→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange→Marlinstone; Orchard→CAM; Apron Sensors→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove, Quartzline.

New part:
S221: All material resequencing decisions are recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the reason, affected aircraft, coordinating parties, and time of approval.
S222: The Audit Event Ledger retains movement updates from the Ramp Movement Board so that post-event review can compare planned sequencing with actual apron performance.
S223: Slot allocation within the Regional Flow Platform is governed by operational safety, published capacity, equitable access, and traceable collaborative decision making.
S224: The Slot Allocation Engine is introduced in operating documentation with the local alias Blueharbor for controller-facing references during transition training.
S225: The Slot Allocation Engine proposes regulated departure and arrival opportunities by matching demand from the Demand Prediction Service to constraints supplied by the Capacity Assessment Module.
S226: The primary inputs are the Flight Intent Message, the Airport Capacity Plan, the current Airport Acceptance Rate, runway metering limits, and airspace sector loading conditions.
S227: When a Ground Delay Program is active, the engine derives a Calculated Takeoff Time or arrival opportunity that preserves the declared capacity envelope before local preference is applied.
S228: The Regional Flow Manager owns the final operating policy for priority classes and may authorize temporary rule changes during a Capacity Reduction State.
S229: The Slot Coordinator administers the allocation run, reviews exceptions, and confirms that proposed results are ready for publication through the Airport CDM Portal.
S230: Baseline priority is assigned first to safety-critical, emergency, humanitarian, and national obligation flights, subject to validation by the appropriate operational authority.
S231: Scheduled commercial services are then handled according to the published timetable, declared readiness, airport acceptance capacity, and the fairness rules held in the Business Rules Registry.
S232: General aviation, repositioning, training, and discretionary movements are allocated after protected and scheduled demand unless a specific operational justification is approved.
S233: Fairness is measured across operators by delay distribution, proportional access to constrained capacity, and avoidance of systematic disadvantage over the active regulation period.
S234: The engine shall not improve one operator's position by imposing an excessive delay on another operator unless the rule basis is visible and logged.
S235: The Airline Interface Adapter supplies operator preferences, but those preferences are advisory unless they are consistent with the governing priority class and available capacity.
S236: The Target Off Block Time is used to test readiness, and an aircraft that cannot meet readiness criteria may be resequenced behind aircraft that can use the opportunity.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
